findings.reason: without the supersession recorded, the two sections state opposite deliverables, and whichever lands second contradicts the plan's own text with no record of it.
findings.text: §13 turns the stall verdict into a new obligations row kind while §7 (declared dependency, plan.html:124) states the stall "reaches the request's own session through the existing needs-you rows … and not through a new obligations row", and closes with "no new row kind is added"; nothing in the plan records that §13 supersedes that interface, so a §7 node lands a needs_you stall row that §13 immediately retires, under an interface statement §13 reverses

findings.reason: a §7 node is free to land a differently named constant or no shared reader, leaving §13's brief unsatisfiable as written or forcing a second parser that its own "fourth parser" rule forbids.
findings.text: §13 requires "the stall verdict (`queue_admission.STALL_VERDICT`)" and "the verdict reader §7 landed", but no `STALL_VERDICT` symbol exists in the tree and §7 never names either the constant or a verdict reader, so the section requires a name its own dependency never binds

findings.reason: the gap is independently true (no production importer was found) so the mechanism stands; only the citation needs replacing with the measurement itself.
findings.text: the section's Why asserts "§7's own review recorded the gap", but the two recorded §7 reviews (plan.html:269, plan.html:272) report the drain view's stuck rule and a missing drain-view test and say nothing about `needs_you` having no production caller

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §13 rests on `queue_admission.STALL_VERDICT` and "the verdict reader §7 landed", neither of which exists in the tree nor is declared by §7, the section it depends on.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §13 names four measurable arms (stalled row with age and stage, plain run-queued row without the verdict, a later launch verdict clears it, one verdict-log read per build) and a declared negative control that drops the stall check so the stalled case fails.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — no gate or evidence log is written to a scratchpad or node-local path; the landing records the close comments cite sit under `docs/evidence/archive/` in the repository and all seven anchors resolve.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `STALL_VERDICT`, `QUEUED_RUN_DUTY_KIND` and the new test name the mechanism; no stage label, ticket number or version tag is introduced, and the cross-plan section citation is a plan reference rather than a code label.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the root cause §13 states is correct on every check — no production importer of `needs_you`, the `run-queued` row at `obligations.py:705` cannot distinguish a stalled request, and the mechanism runs on the real hook path through `_queued_item` — but the section's citation "§7's own review recorded the gap" does not resolve to any recorded §7 review.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s13 has one goal, a stalled request appearing as a stalled obligations row; removing the needs_you stall rows is the retirement of the surface that row replaces, not an independent second deliverable, and deletion of the module is guarded by "if nothing else calls it".
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §13 declares `depends-on` s7 and then delivers a stalled obligations row that §7's own interface line explicitly rules out ("not through a new obligations row … no new row kind is added", plan.html:124), with no decision, followup or amendment recording that §13 supersedes it.
